title.value: Doubly Right Object Recognition: A Why Prompt for Visual Rationales
title.justification: The paper focuses on a new benchmark and method for object recognition, particularly evaluating visual models on both correct predictions and rationales.
title.quote: In this paper, we investigate whether computer vision models can also provide correct rationales for their predictions. We propose a “doubly right” object recognition benchmark, where the metric requires the model to simultaneously produce both the right labels as well as the right rationales.

extractions.description: This paper introduces a benchmark for "doubly right" object recognition, where computer vision models must predict both correct categorical labels and correct rationales. It evaluates state-of-the-art models like CLIP on their ability to provide correct rationales and proposes a framework to transfer rationale generation from language models to visual domains, using prompts.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: The central focus of the paper is the development of visual prompts to improve model interpretability, which does not directly address climate or ecological sustainability.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: We find that state-of-the-art visual models, such as CLIP, often provide incorrect rationales for their categorical predictions. However, by transferring the rationales from language models into visual representations through a tailored dataset, we show that we can learn a “why prompt,” which adapts large visual representations to produce correct rationales.

primary_category.justification: The paper focuses on methodologies in computer vision, discussing how models provide rationales rather than directly targeting climate or ecologically-related sustainable development goals.
primary_category.quote: Learning models that can explain their own decision is important for building trustworthy systems, especially in applications that require human-machine interactions.

secondary_categories.justification: There are no secondary themes in the paper that relate to climate or ecologically-related sustainable development.
secondary_categories.quote: We propose to leverage this external knowledge from web search engines, a larger-scale knowledge base than Wiktionary.

primary_sub_category.justification: The study is centered around visual model interpretability, having no alignment with sustainability-focused sub-categories.
primary_sub_category.quote: Our paper first introduces a benchmark for doubly right object recognition, where computer vision models must predict both correct categorical labels as well as correct rationales.

secondary_sub_categories.justification: The sub-topics primarily deal with techniques in computer vision, not addressing any specific sustainability-related applications.
secondary_sub_categories.quote: Instead, we propose a framework to explicitly transfer the chain-of-thought reasoning from NLP models into vision models.

applications.justification: The paper doesn't apply its research directly to sustainability-focused applications.
applications.quote: Visual recognition models achieve high performance on the classification tasks, yet they often provide vague and unreliable interpretations and rationales.

new_primary_category.justification: No new category is needed as this work is outside the scope of sustainability-focused themes.
new_primary_category.quote: Visual models often learn spurious correlations without external knowledge.

new_primary_sub_category.justification: There is no need for a new sub-category since the paper does not intersect with sustainability themes.
new_primary_sub_category.quote: Visual reasoning is examined as a core aspect of model performance.
